text: The beauty to founders is they don't need help in the middle. You can be 10 times better in the middle than any sales rep at your bigger competitor.
speaker: Jason Lemkin
context: Lenny asks Jason to clarify what he means by 'middlers' in sales conversations. Jason explains that founders are naturally good at the middle part of sales conversations - they can expertly discuss their product and solve customer problems, even if they're not great at opening or closing deals. He argues that founders have a huge advantage over sales reps at bigger competitors because they have deep product knowledge that most sales reps lack.
text_ko: 창업자(founders)들의 좋은 점은 중간에서는 외부의 도움이 필요 없다는 거예요. 중간에서라면 큰 경쟁사에 있는 어떤 영업 담당자(sales rep)보다도 10배는 더 잘할 수 있어요.
text_zh: 对创始人来说，最棒的是中间环节不用别人帮忙——你在这通常能比那些比你更大的竞争对手的任何一个销售强十倍。
text_es: Lo bueno para los fundadores es que no necesitan ayuda en la fase intermedia. En esa fase pueden ser diez veces mejores que cualquier representante de ventas (sales rep) de su competidor más grande.
key_sentence: You can be 10 times better in the middle than any sales rep at your bigger competitor.
original_text: The beauty to founders is they don't need help in the middle. You can be 10 times better in the middle than any sales rep at your bigger competitor. If you're running, I am just making up CRM, but if you're running a new CRM startup, you can run circles around 98% of the sales reps at Salesforce or HubSpot. They have the brand, they have the partners, they have the integrations, but they cannot answer the questions you can answer.

vocabulary.definition: A competitor is a company or individual that operates in the same market and offers similar products or services, vying for the same customer base.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, understanding competitors is crucial for strategic planning, market analysis, and positioning products effectively to gain a competitive advantage.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'competitor' is a neutral term, it can carry a negative connotation in contexts where aggressive rivalry is emphasized.

vocabulary.definition: A sales rep, or sales representative, is an individual responsible for selling a company's products or services, often acting as a liaison between the company and its customers.
vocabulary.businessContext: Sales reps play a vital role in driving revenue, building customer relationships, and providing feedback to the company about market trends and customer needs.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'sales rep' is often used informally, while 'sales executive' might be preferred in more formal contexts.

vocabulary.definition: Founders are individuals who establish a company or organization, often taking on significant risk and responsibility in the early stages of development.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the startup ecosystem, founders are crucial as they drive the vision, culture, and initial strategy of the business, often seeking funding and building a team.
vocabulary.nuance: The term 'founders' carries a sense of innovation and entrepreneurship, but can imply a lack of experience in larger corporate environments.

text: Those first couple reps have to be people you would buy your own product from. That's it. Now we can talk about other criteria. We can talk about normalizing for deal size. We can talk about industry expertise.
speaker: Jason Lemkin
context: Lenny asks about signs that indicate it's time to hire your first salesperson. Jason shares his key hiring criterion for the first two sales reps - they must be people you would actually buy your own product from. He explains that most founders will need to interview around 30 candidates, with 20 being completely unprepared and only 1-2 being truly magical hires who understand the product deeply.
text_ko: 처음 몇 명의 영업 담당자(reps)는 당신이 그들에게서 직접 제품을 살 만큼 신뢰가 가는 사람이어야 해요. 그게 전부예요. 그다음에 다른 기준들을 얘기할 수 있어요. 거래 규모(deal size)에 맞춰 보정하는 것, 업계 전문성(industry expertise)에 대해서도 이야기할 수 있고요.
text_zh: 最开始招的那几位销售，一定要是你自己也愿意从他们那里买这款产品的人。就这么简单。其他标准可以再说——比如按交易规模做归一(normalizing for deal size)，或者看行业专长(industry expertise)。
text_es: Esos primeros representantes de ventas (reps) tienen que ser personas a las que tú mismo les comprarías tu propio producto. Eso es todo. Ahora ya podemos hablar de otros criterios: podemos hablar de ajustar por el tamaño de los acuerdos (deal size). Podemos hablar de la experiencia en el sector.
key_sentence: First reps must be people you'd buy your own product from to avoid breaking your brain.
original_text: Those first couple reps have to be people you would buy your own product from. That's it. Now we can talk about other criteria. We can talk about normalizing for deal size. We can talk about industry expertise. We can talk about all this kind of stuff, but when you go out as a first time founder and interview 30 reps, and you're going to have to interview 30, and 20 are just going to break your brain because they don't do any work and they don't do any prep and they didn't even go to your website.

vocabulary.definition: Standards or principles by which something is judged or decided.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business settings, criteria are often established to evaluate candidates, proposals, or performance metrics to ensure alignment with organizational goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While 'criteria' is often used in plural form, it can imply a set of standards that are flexible depending on the context of the decision-making process.

vocabulary.definition: A deep understanding and knowledge of a specific industry, including its trends, challenges, and best practices.
vocabulary.businessContext: Having industry expertise is critical for professionals in business, as it enables them to make informed decisions, provide valuable insights, and build credibility with clients and stakeholders.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase often implies not just knowledge, but also experience and a network of contacts within the industry, making it a valuable asset in competitive environments.

text: You need two sales reps hitting quota closing deals before you're ready to hire a manager for them.
speaker: Jason Lemkin
context: Lenny asks about the appropriate level and seniority for first sales hires, specifically about the common mistake of hiring a VP of sales too early. Jason explains that you need two successful individual contributor reps before hiring a sales manager. He describes the VP of sales role as scaling from 3 to 300 reps, not finding initial product-market fit.
text_ko: 매니저를 뽑을 준비가 되려면, 두 명의 영업 담당자(sales reps)가 쿼터(quota)를 꾸준히 달성하면서 거래를 성사시키고 있어야 해요.
text_zh: 在你准备给他们配经理之前，至少要有两名销售能稳定完成配额并成交。
text_es: Antes de contratar a un gerente (manager) que los supervise, necesitas que al menos dos representantes de ventas (sales reps) estén cumpliendo su cuota y cerrando tratos.
key_sentence: You need two sales reps hitting quota before hiring a manager for them starting to repeat.
original_text: You need two sales reps hitting quota closing deals before you're ready to hire a manager for them. Almost all VPs of sales, their job is to take you from rep three to 300, to take you from three to 300, to take something that's just starting to repeat, a script that's just starting to work, leads that are just starting to come in.

vocabulary.definition: A quota is a fixed share or portion that is assigned to an individual or group, often in terms of sales or production targets.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business, quotas are commonly used to set performance benchmarks for sales teams, ensuring that each member contributes to overall revenue goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While quotas can motivate employees to achieve targets, they may also create pressure that can lead to unethical sales practices if not managed properly.

vocabulary.definition: Closing deals refers to the finalization of a business agreement or sale, where all terms are agreed upon and the transaction is completed.
vocabulary.businessContext: In sales environments, closing deals is a critical skill that directly impacts revenue generation and is often the ultimate goal of sales representatives.
vocabulary.nuance: The phrase implies not just the act of completing a sale, but also the ability to negotiate and persuade effectively, making it a key indicator of a salesperson's success.

text: If you hire a VP of sales before then, you're asking them to find product market fit to be the first rep, to be the second rep and scale it all at the same time.
speaker: Jason Lemkin
context: Lenny continues asking about when to hire a VP of sales. Jason emphasizes why hiring a VP of sales too early always fails - you're asking one person to simultaneously discover product-market fit, be the first successful rep, train a second rep, and build scalable processes. He warns that this approach typically results in the VP leaving within eight months and burning through significant cash.
text_ko: 그 전에 영업 부사장(VP of Sales)을 뽑으면, 그 사람에게 제품-시장 적합성(product-market fit)을 찾으라고 하면서 동시에 첫 번째, 두 번째 영업 담당자 역할을 하고 팀을 키우라고 요구하는 셈이에요.
text_zh: 如果在还没找到产品与市场匹配（product market fit）之前就招销售副总裁（VP of Sales），你就是在让他们去找市场契合、亲自当第一、第二个销售代表，同时还得负责把团队和业务做大。
text_es: Si contratas a un VP de ventas (VP of Sales) antes de eso, le estás pidiendo que encuentre el encaje producto-mercado (product-market fit), que haga de primer representante de ventas (sales rep), que actúe como el segundo vendedor y que, además, lo escale todo al mismo tiempo.
key_sentence: you're asking them to find product market fit to be the first rep, to be the second rep and scale it all at the same time.
original_text: If you hire a VP of sales before then, you're asking them to find product market fit to be the first rep, to be the second rep and scale it all at the same time. It's mission impossible to do all four at the same time. So that's the biggest mistake is, Lenny, I can't get sales going at my company. I can't do it, but I raised $4 million in my C+ round. I'm going to go out and hire the VP of sales. That VP of sales will not be there in eight months.

vocabulary.definition: To scale means to increase the capacity or size of a business or its operations in a systematic and efficient manner. This often involves expanding resources, production, or market reach to accommodate growth.
vocabulary.businessContext: In the tech industry, scaling is essential for startups that aim to grow rapidly while maintaining operational efficiency. It often involves leveraging technology and processes to handle increased demand without a proportional increase in costs.
vocabulary.nuance: The term implies not just growth, but growth that is sustainable and manageable, distinguishing it from mere expansion which may not be efficient.

vocabulary.definition: Rep is short for representative, typically referring to a salesperson or agent who represents a company or product in the marketplace. They are responsible for engaging with customers and driving sales.
vocabulary.businessContext: In sales organizations, reps play a vital role in customer acquisition and relationship management, often being the first point of contact between the company and potential clients.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry informal connotations, and while it is widely accepted in business contexts, it is less formal than using the full term 'representative'.

text: Here's the mistake that 99% of founders and sales reps make. We're not really selling in B2B, we're solving problems. Our job as sales reps in SaaS is to not sell a used car, okay? We are selling a Tesla Model 3 performance.
speaker: Jason Lemkin
context: During a discussion about interview techniques for sales reps, Jason explains the fundamental mindset shift needed in B2B sales. He argues that SaaS companies aren't selling commodities but solving meaningful problems, comparing it to selling a high-quality Tesla rather than using manipulative used car tactics. This perspective is crucial for both founders and sales reps to understand.
text_ko: 창업자와 영업 담당자 99%가 저지르는 실수가 있어요. 기업 간 거래(B2B)에서는 사실 '판매'하는 게 아니라 문제를 해결하는 거예요. 서비스형 소프트웨어(SaaS) 영업으로서 우리의 역할은 중고차를 파는 사람이 되는 게 아니에요. 우리는 테슬라 모델 3 퍼포먼스(Tesla Model 3 Performance)를 파는 거예요.
text_zh: 有个常见误区，99%的创始人(founders)和销售(sales reps)都会犯：他们把企业对企业(B2B)的销售当成“推东西”。其实不是，我们是在解决问题。作为SaaS(SaaS)的销售，我们的工作不是当二手车推销员——我们卖的是特斯拉(Tesla) Model 3 Performance。
original_text: Here's the mistake that 99% of founders and sales reps make. We're not really selling in B2B, we're solving problems. Our job as sales reps in SaaS is to not sell a used car, okay? We are selling a Tesla Model 3 performance. It has competition, I might not need it this week, but it's pretty darn good. Let me help you get you into that Model 3 performance today.

vocabulary.definition: The process of identifying issues and finding effective solutions to address them.
vocabulary.businessContext: In B2B sales, particularly in SaaS, the focus is often on solving problems for clients rather than merely selling products, emphasizing value creation.
vocabulary.nuance: This phrase suggests a proactive and customer-centric approach, highlighting the importance of understanding client needs over traditional sales tactics.

text: The first three months of a new rep, you're lucky if they can close as much as their take-home pay is, their OT.
speaker: Jason Lemkin
context: Lenny asks about compensation and quota structure for early sales hires. Jason explains his unconventional approach of letting new reps keep 100% of what they close in their first quarter. He acknowledges this isn't immediately profitable but argues it's necessary investment to help reps get started and build confidence while learning the product.
text_ko: 신입 영업사원의 첫 3개월은, 그들이 성사시키는 매출이 본인의 실수령액(OT/OTE, on-target earnings)만큼만 돼도 운이 좋은 편이에요.
text_zh: 一个新来的销售(rep)头三个月，能把业绩做到和他们到手工资(take-home pay)、目标收入(OT)差不多，你就算走运了。
text_es: En los primeros tres meses de un nuevo representante de ventas (rep), tienes suerte si consigue cerrar ventas por lo mismo que se lleva a casa (su OT).
key_sentence: New reps often close only their take-home pay in the first three months, needing investment.
original_text: The first three months of a new rep, you're lucky if they can close as much as their take-home pay is, their OT. And so, in the really early days, my early, early day comp plan is, look, your first three months, you keep a hundred percent of what you close. Of course, that's not profitable for the business, but you've got to invest in them, right?

vocabulary.definition: In a business context, to 'close' refers to the act of finalizing a sale or agreement, effectively converting a potential customer into a paying client.
vocabulary.businessContext: Sales professionals are often evaluated on their ability to close deals, as this directly impacts revenue generation and overall business success.
vocabulary.nuance: The term can carry a sense of urgency and finality; however, it should be used carefully to avoid implying pressure tactics that may alienate clients.

vocabulary.definition: Take-home pay is the amount of money an employee receives after all deductions, such as taxes and benefits, have been subtracted from their gross salary.
vocabulary.businessContext: Understanding take-home pay is essential for employees when assessing their financial situation and for employers when designing compensation packages.
vocabulary.nuance: The term is often used in discussions about salary negotiations and financial planning, emphasizing the net income that employees actually receive.

text: The magical thing at the high level that it compounds, if you have a self-service model, a PLG model, I actually think the number one most important metric is churn. It's going to this churn, churn, churn, churn.
speaker: Jason Lemkin
context: Lenny asks about product teams taking on P&L responsibilities and revenue goals. Jason discusses the importance of focusing on metrics that compound over time rather than short-term revenue optimization. He emphasizes that for PLG companies, churn is the most critical metric because high churn rates (3-4% monthly) are nearly impossible to overcome and prevent building a sustainable billion-dollar business.
text_ko: 큰 그림에서 진짜 마법 같은 건 누적되는 효과예요. 셀프서비스 모델(self-service model)이나 PLG 모델(PLG model)을 운영하고 있다면, 제가 보기엔 가장 중요한 지표는 이탈률(churn)이에요. 결국 계속 이탈, 이탈, 이탈, 이탈이에요.
text_zh: 从高层面看，这事的魔力就是会产生复利效应。如果你走自助式模式(self-service model)或产品驱动增长(PLG model)，我真觉得最重要的指标就是流失率(churn)。说白了就是一直在流失、流失、流失。
text_es: Lo mágico, a grandes rasgos, es que se va acumulando: si tienes un modelo de autoservicio (self-service) o un modelo PLG (product-led growth), yo diría que la métrica número uno es la tasa de abandono (churn). Al final va a ser churn, churn, churn, churn.
key_sentence: Churn is the most important metric; if not top decile, it's almost unsolvable.
original_text: The magical thing at the high level that it compounds, if you have a self-service model, a PLG model, I actually think the number one most important metric is churn. It's going to this churn, churn, churn, churn. And when I meet any startup for investing or anything, if the churn is not top decile for a low end product, I'm always out. It's almost unsolvable.

vocabulary.definition: A self-service model is a business approach that allows customers to access products or services independently, without direct assistance from staff.
vocabulary.businessContext: In tech and startups, this model is often employed to enhance user experience and reduce operational costs by enabling customers to manage their own interactions with the product.
vocabulary.nuance: This term conveys a sense of empowerment for the customer, but may imply a lack of personal touch or support from the company.

vocabulary.definition: A metric is a standard of measurement used to assess performance, progress, or success in a specific area.
vocabulary.businessContext: In business and tech, metrics are critical for evaluating the effectiveness of strategies, guiding decision-making, and measuring outcomes against goals.
vocabulary.nuance: While metrics are essential for data-driven decision-making, relying solely on them can overlook qualitative factors that also influence success.

vocabulary.definition: Churn refers to the rate at which customers stop doing business with a company or discontinue using its services.
vocabulary.businessContext: In subscription-based models, monitoring churn is vital for understanding customer retention and overall business health, as high churn rates can indicate dissatisfaction or competitive pressures.
vocabulary.nuance: Churn can carry a negative connotation, suggesting a failure to meet customer needs, and is often a key focus for improvement in customer experience strategies.
